title: DeciderSettings
description: Data file content/decider/settings.json: when inhabitants ask the decider (W1595: whatever an inhabitant does not understand becomes a question to the AI; B2487: questions wait without a fixed time limit), and the environment values used until weather (B2) and temperature (B5) exist. Placeholders until Marcel decides.

deadline_ms.description: Service time budget per request (ADR-0006); the core itself never waits for the clock.

max_open_questions.description: Open questions per inhabitant at the same time, whether with the decider or waiting (held back, or for the night). A question of a trigger that interrupts is not kept out by questions that only wait.

retry_after_minutes.description: After a retryable ServiceError the question stays open and is sent again after this many game minutes (B2487: no fixed time limit).

request_log_full_hours.description: A1750 (B2768): game hours a request stays whole in the decision and job logs; older ones keep only a fingerprint (sha256 and length) - the replay needs only the answers, commands and that fingerprint. Absent = every request stays whole.

ask_cooldown_hours.description: Game hours before the same inhabitant asks about the same subject again.

choice_protection_hours.description: One thing at a time (A1487): while a question of an inhabitant is with the decider, or a choice the decider made for it is queued or under way (walking there or doing it), no further question of that inhabitant goes to the decider - it opens with its question mark and is asked once the inhabitant is free again, if what raised it still holds (the thing or the other still in sight and not understood); otherwise it lapses (question_failed, detail lapsed) and the trigger raises it anew when it sees the thing again. This value is the time limit in game hours: it bounds what has no end of its own - a question that is out with the decider, the walk to a chosen target, a choice queued behind a walk; older than this they no longer hold anything back. An action that runs ends by its duration, and with it the wait of a choice queued behind it, so these need no limit. Exceptions: triggers with interrupts, and a choice that serves none of the needs below their neglect_below (inhabitant model). Omitted or 0 = questions are never held back (as before).

max_requests_per_step.description: At most this many requests go to the decider in one step (tick), whatever raised them: new questions, questions that waited (held back) and questions sent again after an error or after loading a save. What is over waits with its question mark and goes out in the next steps, in the order it would have gone. The places of a step are taken in this order: questions due to be sent again (after an error or a load), then questions that waited, then new ones - so while the AI service keeps failing, retries can fill a step and the others wait longer. Bounds the one step in which many questions fall due together - all held-back questions at the end of choice_protection_hours, every open question after loading a save. Omitted = no limit (as before).

unknown_inhabitant_max_asks.description: How often an inhabitant asks who the same other inhabitant is (trigger unknown_inhabitant) while it never learns the name; omitted = no limit.

failures.description: A1778 (B2814, Marcel W2204): an action that fails at the core - whatever the reason (too far, too high, too smooth, no step, the listener asleep, ...) - becomes an open question with its question mark: the situation (action, kind of target, reason code, place) goes to the decider with the usual options (trigger action_failed), and the action rests on that target for rest_hours. Once per action, kind of target and reason within ask_again_after_hours. Omitted = a failure asks nothing.

ThroughputSettings.description: A1587 (B7 R24, R26, R28; B2804, D1161): how much the AI may be asked by day, by the game's speed and the measured time of one AI job (both logged player commands, so a replay asks the same). Per game hour at most floor(day_share x real seconds of a game hour at the speed / seconds per job) requests go out, at least min_per_hour; a question over it keeps its question mark and goes out later (R25), a talk stays without words, a free moment is not asked. What the player raises (noticed_player) is never held back by it. Omitted = no such limit (as before).

day_share.description: Share of the real time the AI may be busy with day requests (the rest for talks with the player, the night's work and slack).

fallback_job_ms.description: Milliseconds one AI job is taken to need while the service has not measured yet (no set_ai_rate).

min_per_hour.description: At least this many requests per game hour whatever the speed, so the followed inhabitant still thinks and talks at the fastest speed (B2804).

answer_within_minutes.description: Game minutes a decision may take (R28): the request's deadline_ms is the real time of these minutes at the current speed, at most deadline_ms; the service does not begin what cannot finish in time.

LeisureSettings.description: Trigger leisure (B2663, D333 v7 boredom -> wish, B2610): an awake inhabitant with no open question, none of whose pressing needs (those with a neglect threshold in the inhabitant model: hunger, thirst, sleep ...) is below needs_at_least - fun, company and purpose do not count, low fun is what makes it bored - whose mood is at least mood_at_least, asks the decider at most every every_hours game hours what to do now; the options are the core's, the choice and the thought the AI's. By day, with or without learning by day: nothing new is learned. Omitted = no leisure questions.

mood.description: A mood that must be at least mood_at_least (e.g. boredom); omitted = any free moment counts.

every_hours.description: Least game hours between two leisure questions of one inhabitant - the free moment's own cool-down; ask_cooldown_hours does not apply to it (D1086), so a value below it is possible.

every_hours_by_trait.description: D1086: every_hours is divided by this trait factor (a higher factor = free moments come more often). Omitted = the same for all.

needs_at_least_by_trait.description: D1086: needs_at_least is multiplied by this trait factor (a lower factor = a free moment already with less strength). Omitted = the same for all.

Trigger.description: A kind of not-understanding that becomes a question.

kind.description: unknown_object: a thing of a type without any belief in sight; noticed_player: the player noticed (click); unknown_inhabitant: another inhabitant in sight whose own name it does not know (B4a R8); leisure: nothing presses the inhabitant and it is bored (B2663, conditions in leisure). action_failed: an action of the inhabitant failed at the core (A1778, B2814, conditions in failures).

ask.description: When the question goes to the AI (A1487): immediate = to the decider the moment it opens (as before); night = it opens with its question mark, is not sent to the decider by day and is answered by the compute night's question job (knowledge settings: night_questions must list the trigger; only for questions about an object type). Omitted = immediate. A later value will follow the day's contingent (D713).

interrupts.description: Whether a question of this trigger goes to the decider even while its inhabitant is busy with another question or an accepted choice (choice_protection_hours); its answer then replaces that choice, as before. Omitted = false: the question waits.

event_kinds.description: Event kinds that are a failed action (vocabulary events); their detail is the reason code.

transient_reasons.description: Reason codes that pass by themselves (woken up, kept awake by a need, a way briefly taken): no question, no rest. Matched on the code before a slash. An event without a reason (the thing is gone) asks nothing either.

rest_only_reasons.description: Reason codes that rest the action on its target but ask nothing (TL B2821: blocked - a jammed way; the rest turns them to another target, a question per jam would be noise). Omitted = none.

rest_hours.description: Game hours the failed action rests on that target (or here, without one).

ask_again_after_hours.description: Game hours before the same failure (action, kind of target, reason) is asked about again.
